title: The 1st of October
subject: One picture, every reason to celebrate
blurb: Every one of these is a real thing somebody celebrates on the 1st of October - and some of them are birthdays. They are all in the picture. Name the missing word in each.

items.spot: An older figure with white hair, leaning on a walking stick.
items.hint: Seven letters. The UN's careful word for people, used here to avoid saying the other thing.

items.spot: Three roasted beans, each with a split down the middle.
items.hint: Six letters. The Americans had theirs two days ago; this is everyone else's.
items.note: Set by the International Coffee Organization in 2015.

items.spot: A large green cabbage or lettuce, with a tomato and an orange beside it.
items.hint: Ten letters. No meat. It opens a whole month of the same.
items.note: Started in 1977 by the North American Vegetarian Society.

items.template: National Day of the People's Republic of ___
items.spot: A red flag with one large gold star and four small ones.
items.hint: Five letters. The republic was proclaimed in Tiananmen Square in 1949, and the holiday runs a whole week.

items.template: Independence Day in ___, free from Britain since 1960
items.spot: A flag in three vertical bands, green, white, green.
items.hint: Seven letters. Africa's most populous country.
items.note: The green is for its farmland, the white for peace.

items.template: Born today in 1935: Julie ___, who came in on an umbrella
items.spot: An open umbrella with a curved handle.
items.hint: Seven letters. Mary Poppins and Maria von Trapp were both her.
items.note: She won the Oscar for Mary Poppins in her first film role.

items.template: Born today in 1930: Richard ___, the first Dumbledore
items.spot: A tall pointed wizard's hat with stars on it, and a white beard below.
items.hint: Six letters. An Irish actor who played the headmaster in the first two Potter films, and sang MacArthur Park.
items.note: He took the part because his granddaughter threatened never to speak to him again.

items.spot: A black dog with floppy ears and a wagging tail.
items.hint: Three letters. Black ones wait longest in rescue centres, which is what the day is about.

items.template: Born today in 1989: Brie ___, who played Captain Marvel
items.spot: A large red star with a gold star inside it.
items.hint: Six letters. She won an Oscar for Room before she put the suit on.
Five letters. Yehudi Menuhin set this one up through the International Music Council.

items.spot: A fat orange gourd with a green stalk and a curling vine.
items.hint: Seven letters. The flavour that takes over every coffee shop from about now until Christmas.
items.note: There is famously none of it in the spice mix.

items.template: Born today in 1924: Jimmy ___, peanut farmer and president
items.spot: A single peanut in its shell.
items.hint: Six letters. The 39th US president, who won the Nobel Peace Prize twenty years after leaving office and lived to a hundred.
items.note: He ran the family peanut farm in Plains, Georgia.
